dog.description_text:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.

Pre-Screener Form

Bearstein is at risk due to behavioral concerns. In the care center, he has demonstrated reactivity toward other dogs, including pulling strongly toward them, becoming tense, and vocalizing, with limited ability to be redirected once aroused. During his Straycation, Bearstein was reported to charge and bark at individuals who approached his preferred person. He also exhibited signs of separation related distress, such as persistent vocalizing and scratching or biting at barriers and doors when separated from people. According to his Borough Breakers report, Bearstein is an energetic, sensitive, and curious dog. In the care center, he is noted to seek out human interaction, leaning into petting and actively soliciting attention from handlers. Medically, Bearstein is Apparently Healthy.

Bearstein came to ACC as a stray. Because of this, we do not know how he is in a home environment. During his time in the care center, Bearstein has shown high levels of fear, resulting in him growling and snapping. When on a straycation, he showed significant separation anxiety, resulting in him scratching and biting doors that separated him from people along with constant barking and crying in the crate. He is noted to charge and bark at people approaching him when he is with his person. He is noted to be high energy and have a high prey drive towards small animals, and with his strength he is hard to redirect. Bearstein is described as an incredibly sweet dog who loves to give kisses and cuddle. We recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

My straycation buddy writes:
Bearstein is a big guy with a big heart! He's looking for his very own person, one who will give him lots of structure, training, love, and snacks. Bearstein loves to go on long walks and sniff around the city, followed by long naps where he'll change positions multiple times, each more adorable than the last. He loves chews and frozen Kongs, but most of all he just wants to be near you!
dog.name: Bearstein
